A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TIPS and retain matching methods, experiments, and appendices. The complete text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including the expanded appendix in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original TIPS evaluations, caption and loss ablations, dataset-curation experiments, and novel-view synthesis results in Tables 1–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds released-model evaluations, DataComp experiments, design ablations, and attention-map analyses.

M1.justification: The core dual-embedding architecture and contrastive, self-distillation, and masking objectives remain unchanged. Appendix A.1 adds a genuine training adaptation for smaller models: a frozen pretrained TIPS-g teacher distills ViT-S/B/L/SO students, followed by high-resolution training. This extends the existing framework without replacing its central method.

E1.justification: v2 adds training on a separately curated DataComp corpus containing 115M image-text pairs. It also evaluates released variants without Mapillary street-level imagery while retaining the original variants. Coverage remains within web image-text pretraining and the existing downstream datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds MaskCLIP-B/14 to COCO/Flickr retrieval and ImageNet zero-shot comparisons; the previous comparators remain. New Table 11 also compares successive CLIP-to-MIM training against the joint training approach.

E3.justification: The existing downstream evaluation protocols are retained, but v2 substantially extends the experimental design. Added experiments evaluate four distilled backbone sizes and vary masking ratios, masking patterns, augmentations, and sequential versus joint training. Appendix A.6 introduces a 500-image COCO sample, attention-concentration metrics, and median-filtered attention-map comparisons.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained caption and dataset-curation ablations, v2 tests dependence on the training-data source, masking and augmentation choices, and successive versus simultaneous objectives in Tables 10–11. Appendix A.6 and Figures 7–8 newly investigate whether the two embeddings exhibit different attention patterns, substantially expanding mechanism and sensitivity analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 8's new distributions summarize per-image attention metrics; the standard deviations measure spatial attention concentration rather than uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for released and distilled models, DataComp training, design ablations, and attention behavior. Table 2 also revises the existing TIPS-g/14 LR segmentation scores from 82.8 to 82.9 on PASCAL and 47.4 to 47.8 on ADE20k. New Table 10 reports DataComp segmentation of 79.1 for TIPS versus 64.3 for CLIP, but KNN accuracy of 73.4 versus 76.0; these are added experimental results, not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The embedding definitions, loss equations (1)–(2), and combined objective are retained. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations appear; the added attention metrics serve empirical analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: combining noisy and synthetic captions through dual embeddings, and combining contrastive learning with self-distillation and masked modeling for general-purpose frozen representations. The release announcement and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of smaller-model capacity and distillation, masking and augmentation trade-offs, and attention specialization through reduced concentration on global proxy patches. It also interprets DataComp results as evidence that gains arise from the method rather than WebLI specifically, although Table 10's KNN regression qualifies that interpretation.

D1.justification: Unlike v1, v2 provides a project address and announces code and six released models. It adds model parameter counts, teacher/student initialization and freezing details, DataComp curation instructions, and an explicit 75% default masking ratio. These materially expand access and reproducibility information while retaining the original hardware and optimization details.

R1.justification: Sections 2 and 3.2 add MaskCLIP alongside SILC and clarify that TIPS combines their respective masked-modeling and self-distillation ingredients. Additional citations support DataComp, BYOL augmentations, knowledge distillation, SO architectures, and global proxy patches. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 makes local wording and terminology edits, explains the [rel] designation, adds the ICLR publication header, extends Appendix A.1, and introduces Appendix A.6 without substantially reorganizing the central narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds model-size and performance Tables 5–7, DataComp Table 10, design-ablation Table 11, and attention Figures 7–8. Tables 2–3 expand with released-model rows, and Table 3 gains MaskCLIP. Existing appendix tables are retained and renumbered, while Figures 1–6 reuse their visual content with layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation and practical usefulness: DataComp experiments test dependence on the original training source, Table 11 examines previously untested design choices, and Appendix A.6 investigates the dual-embedding mechanism. Smaller-model evaluations and the reported code/model release address important accessibility gaps in v1. The DataComp discussion underplays the KNN regression from CLIP's 76.0 to TIPS's 73.4, but this localized interpretive weakness does not outweigh the broader gains in evidence and reproducibility information.
